title: POS System
description: A Django-based Point of Sale system covering inventory, sales, staff scheduling, clock-in/out tracking, and business reporting — started after watching a commercial POS system fail at two different bars I worked at: inventory drifted out of sync and sales periodically didn't register. Built from the ground up to understand where that kind of software actually breaks.
features: Concurrency-safe checkout using select_for_update() and F() expressions to prevent overselling when multiple sales hit the same product at once.
Role-based staff access (Admin / Manager / Staff) with clock-in/out tracking and manager-created shift scheduling.
Sales reporting with revenue totals, top products, and gross margin breakdowns computed via Django ORM aggregation.
Service-layer architecture — business logic lives in SaleService/ShiftService, not views — split across focused Django apps (inventory, sales, staff, users, reports).

logs.event: Started as a self-taught side project after experiencing a commercial POS system fail firsthand as a bartender — inventory counts drifted and sales periodically didn't register. Used a break from that job to learn Django (first web app, prior experience was Python scripting only) and get a bare-bones data model and login flow working.

Picked the project back up after hitting the same class of failures with the same software while coaching at a different bar. Expanded the data model to support inventory tracking and multiple user accounts — still no UI at this stage.
Returned with more focused effort: built the first UI and started treating it as more than a personal practice project.
Initial baseline audit — identified security gaps and architectural issues in the original single-app implementation
Refactored into focused Django apps with a service-layer architecture and role-based permissions
Security hardening, environment-based config, and GitHub-readiness pass completed; full test suite passing
